4.text: SE Question 47: He made a career out of ________ arguments and fictional lab results, but lost his job and reputation when his lies were exposed by an article in The New York Times.
4.explanation: 'specious' and 'spurious' form the correct pair. 'specious' means plausible but false; 'spurious' means plausible but false.

4.text: SE Question 48: Despite an ________ beginning, Mike's road trip became a series of mishaps, and he was soon stranded and penniless, leaning against his wrecked automobile.
4.explanation: 'auspicious' and 'propitious' form the correct pair. 'auspicious' means favorable, the opposite of sinister; 'propitious' means presenting favorable circumstances; likely to result in or show signs of success The child's heartbeat is still weak, but I am seeing many propitious signs and I think that she may be healing.

4.text: SE Question 49: As all of the other campers cowered in their tents, Bill, armed only with a flashlight, ________ tracked down the bear that had raided their food.
4.explanation: 'audacious' and 'intrepid' form the correct pair. 'audacious' means willing to be bold in social situations or to take risks; 'intrepid' means fearless.

4.text: SE Question 50: The professor used such ________ expression that many students in the class either fell asleep from bordeom or stayed awake to complete his sentences and humor friends.
4.explanation: 'banal' and 'trite' form the correct pair. 'banal' means repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse; 'trite' means repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse.

4.text: SE Question 51: The lifespan of a mayfly is ________, lasting from a few hours to a couple of days.
4.explanation: 'ephemeral' and 'transitory' form the correct pair. 'ephemeral' means lasting a very short time; 'transitory' means lasting a very short time.

4.text: SE Question 52: Map collecting is an ________ hobby to most, but to geography geeks it is a highly enjoyable pasttime.
4.explanation: 'esoteric' and 'recondite' form the correct pair. 'esoteric' means confined to and understandable by only an enlightened inner circle; 'recondite' means difficult to penetrate; incomprehensible to one of ordinary understanding or knowledge.

4.text: SE Question 53: Amy's name was very apt: she was so ________ that she was twice voted class president.
4.explanation: 'amiable' and 'genial' form the correct pair. 'amiable' means friendly; 'genial' means agreeable, conducive to comfort.

4.text: SE Question 54: Monte was no miser, but was simply ________, wisely spending the little that he earned.
4.explanation: 'frugal' and 'thrifty' form the correct pair. 'frugal' means not spending much money (but spending wisely); 'thrifty' means spending money wisely.

4.text: SE Question 55: Showing no patience, the manager utterly ________ the sales team that lost the big account.
4.explanation: 'lambast' and 'rebuke' form the correct pair. 'lambast' means criticize severely or angrily; 'rebuke' means criticize severely or angrily; censure.

4.text: SE Question 56: The movie director was known for hiring beautiful actors in order to deflect attention away from the ________ scripts he would typically use.
4.explanation: 'insipid' and 'jejune' form the correct pair. 'insipid' means dull and uninteresting; 'jejune' means immature; childish.

4.text: SE Question 57: Despite the president's seemingly ________ speeches, he was a skilled and ruthless negotiator.
4.explanation: 'artless' and 'ingenuous' form the correct pair. 'artless' means without cunning or deceit; 'ingenuous' means to be naÃ ̄ve and innocent.

4.text: SE Question 58: Most lottery winners go from being conservative, frugal types to outright ________ who blow millions on fast cars, lavish homes, and giant yachts.
4.explanation: 'profligate' and 'spendthrift' form the correct pair. 'profligate' means someone who spends money recklessly or wastefully; 'spendthrift' means one who spends money extravagantly.

4.text: SE Question 59: Her boss further cemented his reuptation for being ________ after throwing a fit when the water cooler wasn't refilled.
4.explanation: 'jejune' and 'puerile' form the correct pair. 'jejune' means immature; childish; 'puerile' means of or characteristic of a child; displaying or suggesting a lack of maturity.

4.text: SE Question 60: Betty is a ________ young woman: everyone she meets is put at ease by her elegance and grace.
4.explanation: 'affable' and 'genial' form the correct pair. 'affable' means likeable; easy to talk to; 'genial' means agreeable, conducive to comfort.

4.text: SE Question 61: Having grown up in a ________ suburb, Jacob relished life in New York City after moving.
4.explanation: 'humdrum' and 'prosaic' form the correct pair. 'humdrum' means dull and lacking excitement; 'prosaic' means dull and lacking imagination.

4.text: SE Question 62: In a move that hardly could be described as ________, Bert spend his entire savings on a luxurious cruise, knowing that other bills would come due a couple months later.
4.explanation: 'provident' and 'thrifty' form the correct pair. 'provident' means careful in regard to your own interests; providing carefully for the future; 'thrifty' means spending money wisely.

4.text: SE Question 63: My little brother is so ________ that I can convince him to sneak cookies from the cupboard for me.
4.explanation: 'malleable' and 'tractable' form the correct pair. 'malleable' means easily influenced; 'tractable' means readily reacting to suggestions and influences; easily managed (controlled or taught or molded).

4.text: SE Question 64: Stranded in the wilderness for four days, the hiker ________, eating protein bars and nuts.
4.explanation: 'languish' and 'pine' form the correct pair. 'languish' means become feeble; 'pine' means to yearn for.

4.text: SE Question 65: Civil rights icon Rosa Parks will forever be remembered for ________ refusing to give up her seat on a public bus--even after the bus driver insisted, she remained rooted in place.
4.explanation: 'adamant' and 'intransigent' form the correct pair. 'adamant' means refusing to change one's mind; 'intransigent' means unwilling to change one's beliefs or course of action.

4.text: SE Question 66: One of the ________ decrees in place during the emperor's rule is that all citizens pay him weekly homage at his palace.
4.explanation: 'arbitrary' and 'capricious' form the correct pair. 'arbitrary' means based on a random, groundless decision; 'capricious' means determined by chance or impulse or whim rather than by necessity or reason Nearly every month our capricious CEO had a new plan to turn the company around, and none of them worked because we never gave them the time they needed to succeed.

4.text: SE Question 67: When their new roommate sat staring at an oak tree for an hour, Marcia thought it indicated a mental problem, but Jeff assured her it was a harmless ________.
4.explanation: 'foible' and 'idiosyncrasy' form the correct pair. 'foible' means a behavioral attribute that is distinctive and peculiar to an individual; 'idiosyncrasy' means a behavioral attribute that is distinctive and peculiar to an individual.

4.text: SE Question 68: Even with a perfect stranger, Charles was always ________ and would rarely hold anything back.
4.explanation: 'candid' and 'ingenuous' form the correct pair. 'candid' means a straightforward and honest look at something; 'ingenuous' means to be naÃ ̄ve and innocent.

4.text: SE Question 69: The manager was finally fired for his ________ leadership, which often bordered on rude and offensive.
4.explanation: 'autocratic' and 'magisterial' form the correct pair. 'autocratic' means offensively self-assured or given to exercising usually unwarranted power; 'magisterial' means offensively self-assured or given to exercising unwarranted power.

4.text: SE Question 70: While Nan was always engaged in philosophical speculation, her brother was occupied with far more ________ concerns: how to earn a salary and run a household.
4.explanation: 'pedestrian' and 'prosaic' form the correct pair. 'pedestrian' means lacking imagination; 'prosaic' means dull and lacking imagination.

4.text: SE Question 71: Dawson came across as ________ and unapproachable--very rarely did students come to his office hours.
4.explanation: 'choleric' and 'irascible' form the correct pair. 'choleric' means prone to outbursts of temper; easily angered; 'irascible' means quickly aroused to anger.

4.text: SE Question 72: Many modern observers regard Eisenhower as ________, particularly in his accurate prediction of the growth of the military.
4.explanation: 'perspicacious' and 'sagacious' form the correct pair. 'perspicacious' means acutely insightful and wise; 'sagacious' means having good judgement and acute insight.

4.text: SE Question 73: A ________ argument will change the minds of even the most skeptical audience.
4.explanation: 'cogent' and 'telling' form the correct pair. 'cogent' means clear and persuasive; 'telling' means significant and revealing of another factor.

4.text: SE Question 74: As a child, Amy would build pillow castles and pretend they were ________ fotresses.
4.explanation: 'impregnable' and 'inviolable' form the correct pair. 'impregnable' means immune to attack; incapable of being tampered with; 'inviolable' means never to be broken, infringed, or dishonored.

4.text: SE Question 75: Plaque is ________: we cannot see it, but each day it eats away at our enamel, causing cavities and other dental problems.
4.explanation: 'insidious' and 'pernicious' form the correct pair. 'insidious' means working in a subtle but destructive way; 'pernicious' means exceedingly harmful; working or spreading in a hidden and injurious way The most successful viruses are pernicious: an infected person may feel perfectly healthy for several months while incubating and spreading the virus.

4.text: SE Question 76: At its ________, the Roman Empire extended across most of the landmass of Eurasia, a feat not paralleled to the rise of the British Empire in the 18th and 19th century.
4.explanation: 'pinnacle' and 'summit' form the correct pair. 'pinnacle' means the highest point; 'summit' means a meeting of high-level leaders.

4.text: SE Question 77: It came as no surprise to pundits that the President's attempt at re-election floundered; even during his term, support for his policies was ________, with an approval rating jumping anywhere from 30 to 60 percent.
4.explanation: 'erratic' and 'mercurial' form the correct pair. 'erratic' means unpredictable; strange and unconventional; 'mercurial' means (of a person) prone to unexpected and unpredictable changes in mood.

4.text: SE Question 78: Those who imagine America's countryside as a ________ region are often disappointed to learn that much of rural U.S.
4.explanation: 'pastoral' and 'rustic' form the correct pair. 'pastoral' means relating to the countryside in a pleasant sense; 'rustic' means characteristic of rural life; awkwardly simple and provincial.

4.text: SE Question 79: The dictator was known for his ________ speeches, puffing his chest out and using big, important- sounding words.
4.explanation: 'grandiloquent' and 'portentous' form the correct pair. 'grandiloquent' means puffed up with vanity; 'portentous' means ominously prophetic.

4.text: SE Question 80: Entrusted with the prototype to his company's latest smartphone, Larry, during a late night karaoke bout, let the prototype slip into the hands of a rival company--the next day Larry was ________, and then fired.
4.explanation: 'excoriate' and 'objurgate' form the correct pair. 'excoriate' means to criticize very harshly; 'objurgate' means express strong disapproval of.

4.text: SE Question 81: Chopin's ballades are filled with sharp changes in moods--a ________ melody can give way to a lighthearted tempo.
4.explanation: 'dolorous' and 'lachrymose' form the correct pair. 'dolorous' means showing sorrow; 'lachrymose' means showing sorrow.

4.text: SE Question 82: Jesse had mockingly pointed out all of Nancy's faults in front of their friends, publicly ________ the poor girl.
4.explanation: 'degrade' and 'demean' form the correct pair. 'degrade' means reduce in worth or character, usually verbally; 'demean' means to insult; to cause someone to lose dignity or respect.

4.text: SE Question 83: I am surprised by the ________ of fast food chains; this is America and I assumed they were on every street.
4.explanation: 'dearth' and 'paucity' form the correct pair. 'dearth' means a lack or shortage; 'paucity' means a lack of something.

4.text: SE Question 84: When the captain and more than half the officers were sick on the very first night of the voyage, many of the passengers felt this was ________, but the rest of the voyage continued without any problems.
4.explanation: 'portentous' and 'prodigious' form the correct pair. 'portentous' means ominously prophetic; 'prodigious' means so great in size or force or extent as to elicit awe.

4.text: SE Question 85: She was not so ________ as to begrudge the beggar the unwanted crumbs from her dinner plate.
4.explanation: 'base' and 'ignoble' form the correct pair. 'base' means the lowest, class were without any moral principles; 'ignoble' means dishonorable.

4.text: SE Question 86: Widespread ________ among voters led to a very small turnout on election day.
4.explanation: 'apathy' and 'indifference' form the correct pair. 'apathy' means an absence of emotion or enthusiasm; 'indifference' means the trait of seeming not to care.

4.text: SE Question 87: Known for their ________ ways, the Spartans were once the most feared people from Peloponnesus to Persia.
4.explanation: 'bellicose' and 'contentious' form the correct pair. 'bellicose' means warlike; inclined to quarrel; 'contentious' means likely to argue.

4.text: SE Question 88: Though his childhood piano teacher was so ________, Max is thankful now, as a professional pianist.
4.explanation: 'exacting' and 'fastidious' form the correct pair. 'exacting' means requiring and demanding accuracy; 'fastidious' means overly concerned with details; fussy.

4.text: SE Question 89: Dexter, distraught over losing his pet dachshund, Madeline, found the police officer's questions ________--after all, he thought, did she have to pry into such details as to what Madeline's favorite snack was?.
4.explanation: 'impertinent' and 'impudent' form the correct pair. 'impertinent' means being disrespectful; improperly forward or bold; 'impudent' means improperly forward or bold.

4.text: SE Question 90: One way of ________ the GRE is to apply to a grad school that does not require GRE scores.
4.explanation: 'circumvent' and 'elude' form the correct pair. 'circumvent' means cleverly find a way out of one's duties or obligations; 'elude' means escape understanding.

4.text: SE Question 91: Compared to middle school students, who have an untamed wildness about them, high school students are somewhat more ________.
4.explanation: 'docile' and 'tractable' form the correct pair. 'docile' means easily handled or managed; willing to be taught or led or supervised or directed Barnyard animals are considerably more docile than the wild animals; 'tractable' means readily reacting to suggestions and influences; easily managed (controlled or taught or molded).

4.text: SE Question 92: John didn't each much at all during the week he had the flu, so now that he is regaining his health, it's not surpring that he has a ________ appetite.
4.explanation: 'ravenous' and 'voracious' form the correct pair. 'ravenous' means extremely hungry; devouring or craving food in great quantities; 'voracious' means very hungry; approaching an activity with gusto.

4.text: SE Question 93: The unpredictable and ________ nature of deja vu makes it a very difficult phenomenon to study properly.
4.explanation: 'transient' and 'transitory' form the correct pair. 'transient' means lasting a very short time; 'transitory' means lasting a very short time.

4.text: SE Question 94: As a child, I ________ my mother with strings of never-ending questions.
4.explanation: 'exasperate' and 'incense' form the correct pair. 'exasperate' means to irritate intensely; 'incense' means make furious.

4.text: SE Question 95: Maria found her coworkers cell phone ________, because every few minutes it would buzz to life with another text message.
4.explanation: 'nettlesome' and 'petulant' form the correct pair. 'nettlesome' means causing irritation or annoyance; 'petulant' means easily irritated or annoyed.

4.text: SE Question 96: The entire audience erupted in shouts and curses, ________ the penalty card issued by the referee.
4.explanation: 'decry' and 'excoriate' form the correct pair. 'decry' means express strong disapproval of; 'excoriate' means to criticize very harshly.

4.text: SE Question 97: The judge found the defendant's comments ________ to the trial, and summarily dismissed him from the witness stand.
4.explanation: 'immaterial' and 'impertinent' form the correct pair. 'immaterial' means not relevant; 'impertinent' means being disrespectful; improperly forward or bold.

4.text: SE Question 98: Over time, the various tribes ________ into a single common culture with one universal language.
4.explanation: 'coalesce' and 'conflate' form the correct pair. 'coalesce' means fuse or cause to grow together; 'conflate' means mix together different elements or concepts.

4.text: SE Question 99: After Stanley found out he was no longer able to go on vacation with his friends, he sat in his room ________.
4.explanation: 'morose' and 'sullen' form the correct pair. 'morose' means ill-tempered and not inclined to talk; gloomy; 'sullen' means showing a brooding ill humor.

4.text: SE Question 100: Most high school physics teachers find themselves ________ the same point over and over again, since many concepts confuse students.
4.explanation: 'elaborate' and 'expound' form the correct pair. 'elaborate' means explain in more detail; 'expound' means add details or explanation; clarify the meaning; state in depth.

4.text: SE Question 101: Sally's parties are ________ affairs, and instead of the usual beer and music, there is tea and intellectual conversation.
4.explanation: 'decorous' and 'staid' form the correct pair. 'decorous' means characterized by good taste in manners and conduct; 'staid' means characterized by dignity and propriety.

4.text: SE Question 102: The principal of my elementary school was a cold, ________ woman; I could never understand why she chose to work with children.
4.explanation: 'austere' and 'spartan' form the correct pair. 'austere' means harsh in manner of temperament; 'spartan' means unsparing and uncompromising in discipline or judgment; practicing great self- denial.

4.text: SE Question 103: Only after fifteen minutes of brainstorming did Samantha's ideas for the essay ________.
4.explanation: 'crystallize' and 'elucidate' form the correct pair. 'crystallize' means cause to take on a definite and clear shape; 'elucidate' means make clearer and easier to understand.

4.text: SE Question 104: Although Sam was trying to honor Mark's sense of humor, many found it quite ________ that he wore a comic nose and glasses mask to Mark's funeral.
4.explanation: 'flippant' and 'frivolous' form the correct pair. 'flippant' means showing inappropriate levity; 'frivolous' means not serious in content or attitude or behavior.

4.text: SE Question 105: A good scientist should be ________, focusing purely on what the evidence says, without personal attachment.
4.explanation: 'dispassionate' and 'impartial' form the correct pair. 'dispassionate' means unaffected by strong emotion or prejudice; 'impartial' means free from undue bias or preconceived opinions.

4.text: SE Question 106: Though ________ for his wanton abuse of the pantry, Lawrence shrugged off his mother's harsh words, and continued to plow through jars of cookies and boxes of donuts.
4.explanation: 'chastise' and 'objurgate' form the correct pair. 'chastise' means to reprimand harshly; 'objurgate' means express strong disapproval of.

4.text: SE Question 107: Just as those who were alive during the 70's are mortified that they once cavorted about in bellbottoms, many who lived during the 80's are now aghast at the ________ pop songs they used to enjoy--really, just what exactly is a total eclipse of the heart?.
4.explanation: 'maudlin' and 'mawkish' form the correct pair. 'maudlin' means overly emotional and sad; 'mawkish' means overly sentimental to the point that it is disgusting.

4.text: SE Question 108: In a famous ________, Vice President Quayle attempted to correct the spelling of a grade school student, only to find that the child was correct.
4.explanation: 'gaffe' and 'solecism' form the correct pair. 'gaffe' means a socially awkward or tactless act; 'solecism' means a socially awkward or tactless act.

4.text: SE Question 109: No number of pleas and bribes would get him to change his ________ attitude.
4.explanation: 'obdurate' and 'obstinate' form the correct pair. 'obdurate' means stubbornly persistent in changing an opinion or action; 'obstinate' means resistant to guidance or discipline; stubbornly persistent.

4.text: SE Question 110: While the CEO enthusiastically shares his plans and agenda with all who will listen, the CFO is far more ________, rarely revealing his perspective.
4.explanation: 'reticent' and 'taciturn' form the correct pair. 'reticent' means reluctant to draw attention to yourself; temperamentally disinclined to talk When asked about her father, Helen lost her outward enthusiasm and became rather reticent; 'taciturn' means habitually reserved and uncommunicative.

4.text: SE Question 111: Since Maggie's cough syrup, which had expired five years back, was no longer ________, she coughed through the night.
4.explanation: 'efficacious' and 'telling' form the correct pair. 'efficacious' means producing the intended result; 'telling' means significant and revealing of another factor.

4.text: SE Question 112: The Japanese noodle maker was ________ in making his noodles and would never let another person take over the task.
4.explanation: 'meticulous' and 'punctilious' form the correct pair. 'meticulous' means marked by extreme care in treatment of details; 'punctilious' means marked by precise accordance with details.

4.text: SE Question 113: To recieve an R rating, the entire movie was ________ because it contained so much violence and grotesque subject matter.
4.explanation: 'bowdlerize' and 'expurgate' form the correct pair. 'bowdlerize' means edit by omitting or modifying parts considered indelicate; 'expurgate' means to remove objectionable material.

4.text: SE Question 114: Jasmine was sad to admit it, but her fledgling relationship with Jacob did not work out because his culinary tastes were simply too ________; "After all," she quipped on her blog, "he considered Chef Boyardee ethnic food.".
4.explanation: 'parochial' and 'provincial' form the correct pair. 'parochial' means narrowly restricted in scope or outlook; 'provincial' means characteristic of the a limited perspective; not fashionable or sophisticated Maggie's enthusiasm about her high school teams seemed provincial to her college classmates, all of whom were following a nationally ranked college team.

4.text: SE Question 115: The office building had been constructed in a ________ manner, so it did not surprise officials when, during a small earthquake, a large crack emerged on the faÃ§ade of the building.
4.explanation: 'haphazard' and 'slapdash' form the correct pair. 'haphazard' means marked by great carelessness; dependent upon or characterized by chance Many golf courses are designed with great care, but the greens on the county golf course seem entirely haphazard; 'slapdash' means carelessly and hastily put together.

4.text: SE Question 116: The film was incredibly ________, introducing highly likeable characters only to have them succumb to a devastating illnesses by the end of the movie.
4.explanation: 'mawkish' and 'sentimental' form the correct pair. 'mawkish' means overly sentimental to the point that it is disgusting; 'sentimental' means effusively or insincerely emotional, especially in art, music, and literature.

4.text: SE Question 117: The police regularly face dangerous situations, so for a police officer not to wear his bullet-proof vest is ________.
4.explanation: 'foolhardy' and 'rash' form the correct pair. 'foolhardy' means marked by defiant disregard for danger or consequences; 'rash' means marked by defiant disregard for danger or consequences; imprudently incurring risk Although Bruce was able to make the delivery in time with a nightime motorcycle ride in the rain, Susan.

4.text: SE Question 118: Randy played a ________, telling his boss that he would leave at the end of the week if he didn't get a raise.
4.explanation: 'gambit' and 'ploy' form the correct pair. 'gambit' means a manuveur or risk in a game or conversation, designed to secure an advantage; 'ploy' means a clever plan to turn a situation to one's advantage.

4.text: SE Question 119: After drinking two expressos each, the animated couple would ________ loudly, annoying the other patrons in the coffee shop.
4.explanation: 'maunder' and 'palaver' form the correct pair. 'maunder' means speak (about unimportant matters) rapidly and incessantly; 'palaver' means speak (about unimportant matters) rapidly and incessantly.

4.text: SE Question 120: The police chief ________ the two officers whose irresponsible decisions almost led to the deaths of seven innocent by-standers.
4.explanation: 'rebuke' and 'remonstrate' form the correct pair. 'rebuke' means criticize severely or angrily; censure; 'remonstrate' means to make objections while pleading.

4.text: SE Question 121: Helen is ________ with her time, often spending hours at the house of a sick friend.
4.explanation: 'munificent' and 'unstinting' form the correct pair. 'munificent' means very generous; 'unstinting' means very generous.

4.text: SE Question 122: Later in his life, Leo Tolstoy was ________ from the Russian Orthodox Church for his writings that contradicted church doctrine.
4.explanation: 'banish' and 'ostracize' form the correct pair. 'banish' means expel from a community, residence, or location; drive away The most difficult part of the fast was banishing thoughts of food; 'ostracize' means exclude from a community or group.

4.text: SE Question 123: I thought I would finish writing the paper by lunchtime, but a number of urgent interruptions served to ________ my plan.
4.explanation: 'frustrate' and 'thwart' form the correct pair. 'frustrate' means hinder or prevent (the efforts, plans, or desires) of; 'thwart' means hinder or prevent (the efforts, plans, or desires) of.

4.text: SE Question 124: Drill sergeants are known to ________ new recruits so mercilessly that the latter often break down during their first week in training.
4.explanation: 'castigate' and 'chastise' form the correct pair. 'castigate' means to reprimand harshly; 'chastise' means to reprimand harshly.

4.text: SE Question 125: Aunt Betty had ________ notions about marriage, believing that a man should court a woman for at least a year before receiving a kiss.
4.explanation: 'antiquated' and 'archaic' form the correct pair. 'antiquated' means old-fashioned; belonging to an earlier period in time; 'archaic' means so old as to appear to belong to a different period.

4.text: SE Question 126: The boss's ________ manner put off many employees, some of whom quit as soon as they found new jobs.
4.explanation: 'browbeat' and 'hector' form the correct pair. 'browbeat' means be bossy towards; discourage or frighten with threats or a domineering manner During the interrogation, the suspect was browbeaten into signing a false confession; 'hector' means to bully or intimidate.

4.text: SE Question 127: Win or lose, the coach was always ________, never giving the athletes an easy practice or a break.
4.explanation: 'implacable' and 'inexorable' form the correct pair. 'implacable' means incapable of making less angry or hostile; 'inexorable' means impossible to stop or prevent.

4.text: SE Question 128: The exam's passage is ________ with difficult words, words that you may have learned only yesterday.
4.explanation: 'affluent' and 'flush' form the correct pair. 'affluent' means wealthy; 'flush' means to be in abundance.

4.text: SE Question 129: politician ________ in scandal--a welcome phenomenon for those who, having barely finished feasting on the sordid details of one imbroglio, can sink their teeth into a fresh one.
4.explanation: 'embroiled' and 'involved' form the correct pair. 'embroiled' means involved in argument or contention; 'involved' means complicated, and difficult to comprehend.

4.text: SE Question 130: At first, Sarah was going to yell at the boy, but she didn't want to ________ him for telling the truth about the situation.
4.explanation: 'reproach' and 'upbraid' form the correct pair. 'reproach' means to express criticism towards; 'upbraid' means to reproach; to scold.

4.text: SE Question 131: was a tireless ________ for the rights of African-Americans in the United States.Â This word has other definitions but this is the most important one for the GRE.
4.explanation: 'advocate' and 'proponent' form the correct pair. 'advocate' means a person who pleads for a cause or propounds an idea; 'proponent' means a person who pleads for a cause or propounds an idea.

4.text: SE Question 132: The International Food Expo was a ________ of culinary delights: gourmet foods from every continent were under one roof.
4.explanation: 'cornucopia' and 'profusion' form the correct pair. 'cornucopia' means an abundant supply of something good; 'profusion' means the property of being extremely abundant.

4.text: SE Question 133: Her dress was ________ and made her look even more beautiful.
4.explanation: 'becoming' and 'decorous' form the correct pair. 'becoming' means appropriate, and matches nicely; 'decorous' means characterized by good taste in manners and conduct.

4.text: SE Question 134: Whitney is ________ about her shoes, arranging them on a shelf in a specific order, each pair evenly spaced.
4.explanation: 'fastidious' and 'meticulous' form the correct pair. 'fastidious' means overly concerned with details; fussy; 'meticulous' means marked by extreme care in treatment of details.

4.text: SE Question 135: The ________ lives on both sides of the political spectrum, outright shunning anybody whose ideas are not consistent with his own.
4.explanation: 'chauvinist' and 'jingoist' form the correct pair. 'chauvinist' means a person who believes in the superiority of their group; 'jingoist' means a person who thinks that their country should be at war.

4.text: SE Question 136: Eating with elbows on the table is considered ________ in refined circles.
4.explanation: 'indecorous' and 'untoward' form the correct pair. 'indecorous' means not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society; 'untoward' means unfavorable; inconvenient.

4.text: SE Question 137: By the time the colonel ________ his soldiers not to land in enemy territory, a few helicopters had already touched down amid heavy gunfire.
4.explanation: 'countermand' and 'rescind' form the correct pair. 'countermand' means a contrary command cancelling or reversing a previous command; 'rescind' means cancel officially.

4.text: SE Question 138: A good teacher will never ________ his students, but will instead empower them.
4.explanation: 'belittle' and 'denigrate' form the correct pair. 'belittle' means lessen the importance, dignity, or reputation of; 'denigrate' means charge falsely or with malicious intent; attack the good name and reputation of someone.

4.text: SE Question 139: Adults look to kids and envy their ________ nature at times, wishing that they could act without reason and play without limitation.
4.explanation: 'capricious' and 'whimsical' form the correct pair. 'capricious' means determined by chance or impulse or whim rather than by necessity or reason Nearly every month our capricious CEO had a new plan to turn the company around, and none of them worked because we never gave them the time they needed to succeed; 'whimsical' means determined by impulse or whim rather than by necessity or reason.

4.text: SE Question 140: History ________ The Odyssey and The Illiad to Homer, but scholars now debate whether he was a.
4.explanation: 'ascribe' and 'impute' form the correct pair. 'ascribe' means attribute or credit to; 'impute' means attribute (responsibility or fault) to something.

4.text: SE Question 141: Some thermally active fountains spew sulfur fumes--the air around them is sometimes so ________ that many have to plug their noses.
4.explanation: 'malodorous' and 'noisome' form the correct pair. 'malodorous' means having an unpleasant smell; 'noisome' means having an extremely bad smell.

4.text: SE Question 142: His speech was so dense and confusing that many in the audience found it ________.
4.explanation: 'cryptic' and 'inscrutable' form the correct pair. 'cryptic' means mysterious or vague, usually intentionally; 'inscrutable' means not easily understood; unfathomable.

4.text: SE Question 143: I was able to ________ the angry mob of students by promising to bring cookies on Monday.
4.explanation: 'conciliate' and 'placate' form the correct pair. 'conciliate' means to make peace with; 'placate' means cause to be more favorably inclined; gain the good will of.

4.text: SE Question 144: The Spanish conquistadors were known for their ________, plundering Incan land and stealing Incan gold.
4.explanation: 'avarice' and 'cupidity' form the correct pair. 'avarice' means greed (one of the seven deadly sins); 'cupidity' means greed for money.

4.text: SE Question 145: Peggy was unable to ________ her kind friend Jane with the cruel and merciless character Jane played on television.
4.explanation: 'conciliate' and 'reconcile' form the correct pair. 'conciliate' means to make peace with; 'reconcile' means make (one thing) compatible with (another).

4.text: SE Question 146: The efforts of the firefighters running into the burning building were ________.
4.explanation: 'commendable' and 'laudable' form the correct pair. 'commendable' means worthy of high praise; 'laudable' means worthy of high praise.

4.text: SE Question 147: Though Walters writes about physics and time travel, his writing is always ________, so readers with little scientific training can understand difficult concepts.
4.explanation: 'lucid' and 'pellucid' form the correct pair. 'lucid' means (of language) transparently clear; easily understandable; 'pellucid' means transparently clear; easily understandable.

4.text: SE Question 148: Few appreciate the ________ scale of the sun: if hollow, it could contain a million Earths.
4.explanation: 'colossal' and 'prodigious' form the correct pair. 'colossal' means so great in size or force or extent as to elicit awe; 'prodigious' means so great in size or force or extent as to elicit awe.

4.text: SE Question 149: The chairman interpreted Taylor's question about promotions as a ________ remark, but in all innocence Taylor was trying to figure out the company's process.
4.explanation: 'snide' and 'supercilious' form the correct pair. 'snide' means expressive of contempt; derogatory or mocking in an indirect way; 'supercilious' means haughty and disdainful; looking down on others.

4.text: SE Question 150: Chris preferred bland and mild beers, but Bhavin preferred a beer with more ________ flavor.
4.explanation: 'robust' and 'stalwart' form the correct pair. 'robust' means sturdy and strong in form, constitution, or construction; 'stalwart' means dependable; inured to fatigue or hardships.

4.text: SE Question 151: The noble families of England once owned vast expanses of beautiful, ________ land.
4.explanation: 'bucolic' and 'rustic' form the correct pair. 'bucolic' means relating to the pleasant aspects of the country; 'rustic' means characteristic of rural life; awkwardly simple and provincial.

4.text: SE Question 152: Most college fraternities are known for ________ rituals that those hoping to the join the fraterntiy must learn.
4.explanation: 'arcane' and 'esoteric' form the correct pair. 'arcane' means requiring secret or mysterious knowledge; 'esoteric' means confined to and understandable by only an enlightened inner circle.

4.text: SE Question 153: Martinet was ________ in dealing with her class, lording over them like a queen.
4.explanation: 'magisterial' and 'peremptory' form the correct pair. 'magisterial' means offensively self-assured or given to exercising unwarranted power; 'peremptory' means bossy and domineering.

4.text: SE Question 154: The ________ manager didn't believe that any of his subordinates could ever have an insight as brilliant his own.
4.explanation: 'haughty' and 'supercilious' form the correct pair. 'haughty' means having or showing arrogant superiority to and disdain of those one views as unworthy; 'supercilious' means haughty and disdainful; looking down on others.

4.text: SE Question 155: Too many the grass at Wimbledon is ________ and only greater tennis players are able to enjoy a game there.
4.explanation: 'inviolable' and 'inviolate' form the correct pair. 'inviolable' means never to be broken, infringed, or dishonored; 'inviolate' means must be kept sacred.

4.text: SE Question 156: Their large "donations" to the local police department gave the drug cartel the ________ confidence to do their business out in the open.
4.explanation: 'brazen' and 'insolent' form the correct pair. 'brazen' means unrestrained by convention or propriety; 'insolent' means rude and arrogant.

4.text: SE Question 157: Eventually, all parents must ________ control of their growing childrens' educations and allow their offspring some autonomy.
4.explanation: 'cede' and 'concede' form the correct pair. 'cede' means relinquish possession or control over; 'concede' means give over; surrender or relinquish to the physical control of another.

4.text: SE Question 158: She surprised her colleagues by having the ________ to publically criticize the findings of an distinguished scientist.
4.explanation: 'audacity' and 'temerity' form the correct pair. 'audacity' means aggressive boldness in social situations; 'temerity' means fearless daring.

4.text: SE Question 159: The ________ thunder continued and the night was punctuated by cracks of lightning--a surreal sleepless night.
4.explanation: 'intermittent' and 'sporadic' form the correct pair. 'intermittent' means stopping and starting at irregular intervals; 'sporadic' means recurring in scattered and irregular or unpredictable instances.

4.text: SE Question 160: Journalists favor an ________ style of writing, in which no unnecessary words are used and every sentence is as short as possible.
4.explanation: 'economical' and 'thrifty' form the correct pair. 'economical' means avoiding waste, efficient; 'thrifty' means spending money wisely.

4.text: SE Question 161: Nietzsche was known for using ________, sometimes encapsulating a complex philosophical thought in a mere sentence.
4.explanation: 'aphorism' and 'apothegm' form the correct pair. 'aphorism' means a short instructive saying about a general truth; 'apothegm' means a short, pithy instructive saying.

4.text: SE Question 162: Some professors find teaching ________ as having to prepare for lectures and conduct office hours prevents them from focusing on their research.
4.explanation: 'unseemly' and 'untoward' form the correct pair. 'unseemly' means not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society He acted in an unseemly manner, insulting the hostess and then speaking ill of her deceased husband; 'untoward' means unfavorable; inconvenient.

4.text: SE Question 163: The prince's distasteful choice of words ________ not only his own name, but the reputation of the entire royal family.
4.explanation: 'besmirch' and 'denigrate' form the correct pair. 'besmirch' means damage the good name and reputation of someone; 'denigrate' means charge falsely or with malicious intent; attack the good name and reputation of someone.

4.text: SE Question 164: The artist had entered a ________ period, producing three masterpieces in the span of two months.
4.explanation: 'fecund' and 'prolific' form the correct pair. 'fecund' means intellectually productive; 'prolific' means intellectually productive.

4.text: SE Question 165: As a child she was quite ________, but as an adult, she has become an adept dancer.
4.explanation: 'bumbling' and 'maladroit' form the correct pair. 'bumbling' means lacking physical movement skills, especially with the hands Within a week of starting, the bumbling new waiter was unceremoniously fired; 'maladroit' means clumsy.

4.text: SE Question 166: The Internet has unleashed the ________ in many of us; many people post stinging criticism on the comments section underneath newspaper articles or YouTube videos.
4.explanation: 'invective' and 'vitriol' form the correct pair. 'invective' means abusive or denunciatory language; 'vitriol' means abusive or venomous language used to express blame or bitter deep-seated ill will His vitriol spewed forth from a deep-seated racisim that consumed his whole life.

4.text: SE Question 167: Cheryl rolled her eyes when she heard the lecturer's ________ advice to "be true to yourself.".
4.explanation: 'hackneyed' and 'trite' form the correct pair. 'hackneyed' means lacking significance through having been overused; 'trite' means repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse.

4.text: SE Question 168: Jim always preferred a ________ approach to discovering a city: he felt that he could see so many more details while walking.
4.explanation: 'itinerant' and 'peripatetic' form the correct pair. 'itinerant' means traveling from place to place to work Doctors used to be itinerant, traveling between patients' homes; 'peripatetic' means traveling by foot.

4.text: SE Question 169: Hitler, like Napoleon, made the ________ move of invading Russia in winter, suffering even more casualties than Napoleon had.
4.explanation: 'imprudent' and 'rash' form the correct pair. 'imprudent' means not wise; 'rash' means marked by defiant disregard for danger or consequences; imprudently incurring risk Although Bruce was able to make the delivery in time with a nightime motorcycle ride in the rain, Susan.

4.text: SE Question 170: Since his mom was a light sleeper, Timmy had to tiptoe ________ through the entire house, careful to not make the floors creak, until he at last was able to enjoy his plunder: a box of chocolate chip cookies.
4.explanation: 'furtive' and 'surreptitious' form the correct pair. 'furtive' means marked by quiet and caution and secrecy; taking pains to avoid being observed While at work, George and his boss Regina felt the need to be as furtive as possible about their romantic relationship; 'surreptitious' means stealty, taking pains not to be caught or detected.

4.text: SE Question 171: After the sales result, the manager was in an ________ mood, letting several employees leave work early that day.
4.explanation: 'effervescent' and 'scintillating' form the correct pair. 'effervescent' means marked by high spirits or excitement; 'scintillating' means describes someone who is brilliant and lively.

4.text: SE Question 172: In an ________ move, the defendant spoke out of order to say terribly insulting things to the judge.
4.explanation: 'impudent' and 'insolent' form the correct pair. 'impudent' means improperly forward or bold; 'insolent' means rude and arrogant.

4.text: SE Question 173: In giving Marcia a particular ________ response, Paul caused people at every other table in the restaurant to turn around an look at them angrily.
4.explanation: 'blatant' and 'vociferous' form the correct pair. 'blatant' means without any attempt at concealment; completely obvious Allen was often punished in school for blatantly disrespecting teachers; 'vociferous' means conspicuously and offensively loud; given to vehement outcry.

4.text: SE Question 174: The men found him ________, but the women adored his smart clothes and casual attitude.
4.explanation: 'raffish' and 'rakish' form the correct pair. 'raffish' means marked by a carefree unconventionality or disreputableness; 'rakish' means marked by a carefree unconventionality or disreputableness.

4.text: SE Question 175: John preferred to avoid equatorial countries; the intense sun would always leave him ________ after he'd spent the day sightseeing.
4.explanation: 'enervate' and 'unnerve' form the correct pair. 'enervate' means to sap energy from; 'unnerve' means to make nervous or upset.

4.text: SE Question 176: Katie is so ________ that she only buys a pair of socks if all of her other socks have holes in them.
4.explanation: 'parsimonious' and 'penurious' form the correct pair. 'parsimonious' means extremely frugal; miserly; 'penurious' means miserly.

4.text: SE Question 177: Unless you can provide ________ evidence, I will remain skeptical.
4.explanation: 'incontrovertible' and 'irrefutable' form the correct pair. 'incontrovertible' means necessarily or demonstrably true; impossible to deny or disprove; 'irrefutable' means impossible to deny or disprove.

4.text: SE Question 178: The findings of the study were ________--the two researchers had different opinions on what the results signified.
4.explanation: 'equivocal' and 'evasive' form the correct pair. 'equivocal' means confusing or ambiguous; 'evasive' means deliberately vague or ambiguous.

4.text: SE Question 179: In extremely trying times, even the moderately wealthy, after a few turns of ill-fortune, can become ________.
4.explanation: 'impecunious' and 'penurious' form the correct pair. 'impecunious' means lacking money; poor; 'penurious' means miserly.

4.text: SE Question 180: The border of the state is ________ with geographic limits on travel; the east and north are surrounded by a nearly uncrossable river and the south by a desert.
4.explanation: 'commensurate' and 'coterminous' form the correct pair. 'commensurate' means to be in proportion or corresponding in degree or amount The convicted felon's life sentence was commensurate to the heinousness of his crime; 'coterminous' means being of equal extent or scope or duration.

4.text: SE Question 181: The tumor located in your ear lobe seems to be ________ and should not cause you any trouble.
4.explanation: 'benign' and 'genial' form the correct pair. 'benign' means (medicine) not dangerous to health; not recurrent or progressive; 'genial' means agreeable, conducive to comfort.

4.text: SE Question 182: I enjoy reading the Daodejing for its ________ and insightful prose; it always gives me something to think about.
4.explanation: 'pithy' and 'sententious' form the correct pair. 'pithy' means concise and full of meaning; 'sententious' means to be moralizing, usually in a pompous sense.

4.text: SE Question 183: Even after all his success, I found him to be accommodating and ________, sharing with me his "secret tips" on how to gain wealth and make friends.
4.explanation: 'complaisant' and 'obliging' form the correct pair. 'complaisant' means showing a cheerful willingness to do favors for others; 'obliging' means showing a cheerful willingness to do favors for others.

4.text: SE Question 184: Matt wanted to buy stone lions for front of the house, but Cynthia convinced him that such a display would be too ________ for a modest house in an unassuming neighborhood.
4.explanation: 'conspicuous' and 'ostentatious' form the correct pair. 'conspicuous' means without any attempt at concealment; completely obvious; 'ostentatious' means intended to attract notice and impress others; tawdry or vulgar.

4.text: SE Question 185: Used to studious high school students, Martha was unprepared for the ________ Kindgergarteners who neither sat still nor listened to a single word she said.
4.explanation: 'fractious' and 'refractory' form the correct pair. 'fractious' means irritable and is likely to cause disruption; 'refractory' means stubbornly resistant to authority or control.

4.text: SE Question 186: The professor had a remarkable ability make even the most difficult concepts seem ________.
4.explanation: 'limpid' and 'pellucid' form the correct pair. 'limpid' means clarity in terms of expression; 'pellucid' means transparently clear; easily understandable.

4.text: SE Question 187: The professor argued that many statements regarded as wise in previous times, such as the Golden Rule, are now regarded as mere ________.
4.explanation: 'bromide' and 'platitude' form the correct pair. 'bromide' means a trite or obvious remark; 'platitude' means a trite or obvious remark.

4.text: SE Question 188: When Ed first met Ruth, he didn't realize she was so ________, but now that they are three months into their relationship, Ed feels a day doesn't go by in which she isn't whining about some minor issue.
4.explanation: 'peevish' and 'petulant' form the correct pair. 'peevish' means easily irritated or annoyed; 'petulant' means easily irritated or annoyed.

4.text: SE Question 189: Phil gets so involved thinking about Aristotle's arguments that he totally forgets ________ concerns, such as exercising and eating regularly.
4.explanation: 'mundane' and 'quotidian' form the correct pair. 'mundane' means relating to the ordinary world; 'quotidian' means found in the ordinary course of events.

4.text: SE Question 190: Herbert took board games too seriously, often appearing ________ after losing.
4.explanation: 'saturnine' and 'sullen' form the correct pair. 'saturnine' means morose or gloomy; 'sullen' means showing a brooding ill humor.

4.text: SE Question 191: In terms of political change, a ________ oftentimes does little more than make the person speaking red in the face.
4.explanation: 'broadside' and 'tirade' form the correct pair. 'broadside' means a strong verbal attack; 'tirade' means an angry speech.

4.text: SE Question 192: At first the hostess tried ________, praising the benefits of cutlery; when Cecil continued eating with his hands, the hostess told him to use a fork at dinner.
4.explanation: 'inkling' and 'intimation' form the correct pair. 'inkling' means a slight suggestion or vague understanding; 'intimation' means an indirect suggestion.

4.text: SE Question 193: Many adults think that they can lie to children, but kids are smart and know when people are ________.
4.explanation: 'artful' and 'disingenuous' form the correct pair. 'artful' means clever in a cunning way; 'disingenuous' means not straightforward; giving a false appearance of frankness.

4.text: SE Question 194: Because the logic behind McMahon's side of the debate was so ________, his audience came out either completely confused or, worse, feeling they'd been tricked.
4.explanation: 'involved' and 'tortuous' form the correct pair. 'involved' means complicated, and difficult to comprehend; 'tortuous' means marked by repeated turns and bends; not straightforward.

4.text: SE Question 195: Teachers often have trouble being ________ to all of their varied students.
4.explanation: 'equitable' and 'evenhanded' form the correct pair. 'equitable' means fair to all parties as dictated by reason and conscience; 'evenhanded' means without partiality.

4.text: SE Question 196: Email is wonderfully efficient, but once something awkward or damaging has been sent, there is no way to ________ it.
4.explanation: 'abjure' and 'retract' form the correct pair. 'abjure' means formally reject or give up (as a belief); 'retract' means pull inward or towards a center; formally reject or disavow a formerly held belief, usually under pressure.

4.text: SE Question 197: The cynic quipped, "There is not much variance in politicians; they all seem to ________".
4.explanation: 'equivocate' and 'prevaricate' form the correct pair. 'equivocate' means to speak vaguely, usually with the intention to mislead or deceive; 'prevaricate' means to speak in an evasive way.

4.text: SE Question 198: A good captain needs to be ________, continuing to hold the wheel and stay the course even during the most violent storm.
4.explanation: 'staunch' and 'steadfast' form the correct pair. 'staunch' means firm and dependable especially in loyalty; 'steadfast' means marked by firm determination or resolution; not shakable.

4.text: SE Question 199: The plants and animals ________ to Australia are notably different from those indigenous to the U.S-- one look at a duckbill platypus and you know you're not dealing with an opossum.
4.explanation: 'endemic' and 'indigenous' form the correct pair. 'endemic' means native; originating where it is found; 'indigenous' means originating in a certain area.

4.text: SE Question 200: The judge was not ________ since he had been bribed by the witness's family.
4.explanation: 'disinterested' and 'impartial' form the correct pair. 'disinterested' means unbiased; neutral; 'impartial' means free from undue bias or preconceived opinions.

4.text: SE Question 201: Despite many calls for mercy, the judge remained ________, citing strict legal precedence.
4.explanation: 'inexorable' and 'intransigent' form the correct pair. 'inexorable' means impossible to stop or prevent; 'intransigent' means unwilling to change one's beliefs or course of action.

4.text: SE Question 202: Every time Susan comes to the office, Frank ________ as if she were about to fire.
4.explanation: 'fawn' and 'grovel' form the correct pair. 'fawn' means try to gain favor by extreme flattery; 'grovel' means show submission or fear.

4.text: SE Question 203: Nothing can make a person more ________ than a big turkey dinner.
4.explanation: 'languid' and 'lethargic' form the correct pair. 'languid' means not inclined towards physical exertion or effort; slow and relaxed; 'lethargic' means lacking energy.

4.text: SE Question 204: As a ________ bibliophile, one who had turned his house into a veritable library, he shocked his friends when he bought a Kindle.
4.explanation: 'arrant' and 'thoroughgoing' form the correct pair. 'arrant' means complete and wholly (usually modifying a noun with negative connotation); 'thoroughgoing' means very thorough; complete.

4.text: SE Question 205: The two sons, plying their angry father with cheesy neckties for Christmas, were hardly able to ________ him -- the father already had a drawer full of ones he had never worn before or ever planned to.
4.explanation: 'appease' and 'propitiate' form the correct pair. 'appease' means pacify by acceding to the demands of; 'propitiate' means to placate or appease.

4.text: SE Question 206: Those old ________ drinking all day down by the river--they are not going to amount to much.
4.explanation: 'miscreant' and 'reprobate' form the correct pair. 'miscreant' means a person who breaks the law; 'reprobate' means a person who is disapproved of.

4.text: SE Question 207: Every time I call the bank, I receive the same ________ answers about our mortgage and never get a clear response.
4.explanation: 'elusive' and 'evasive' form the correct pair. 'elusive' means difficult to capture or difficult to remember; 'evasive' means deliberately vague or ambiguous.

4.text: SE Question 208: Pete was an ________ student, completing every assignment thoroughly and on time.
4.explanation: 'diligent' and 'industrious' form the correct pair. 'diligent' means characterized by care and perseverance in carrying out tasks; 'industrious' means characterized by hard work and perseverance.

4.text: SE Question 209: In one of the most famous ________ about classical music, Mark Twain said: "Wagner's music is better than it sounds.".
4.explanation: 'epigram' and 'quip' form the correct pair. 'epigram' means a witty saying; 'quip' means a witty saying or remark.

4.text: SE Question 210: The ________ wings of a butterfly, which allow it to fly, are also a curse, so delicate that they are often damaged.
4.explanation: 'ethereal' and 'gossamer' form the correct pair. 'ethereal' means characterized by lightness and insubstantiality; 'gossamer' means characterized by unusual lightness and delicacy.

4.text: SE Question 211: The fact that Ella's moods were as ________ as the weather was problematic for her relationships--it didn't help that she lived in Chicago.
4.explanation: 'fickle' and 'mercurial' form the correct pair. 'fickle' means liable to sudden unpredictable change, esp; 'mercurial' means (of a person) prone to unexpected and unpredictable changes in mood.

4.text: SE Question 212: The lawyer's demands were so ________ that rather than pay an exorbitant sum or submit himself to any other inconveniences, the defendant decided to find a new lawyer.
4.explanation: 'exorbitant' and 'unconscionable' form the correct pair. 'exorbitant' means greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation; 'unconscionable' means unreasonable; unscrupulous; excessive.

4.text: SE Question 213: Paul ________ to his boss so often the boss herself became nauseated by his sycophancy.
4.explanation: 'fawn' and 'kowtow' form the correct pair. 'fawn' means try to gain favor by extreme flattery; 'kowtow' means to bow or act in a subservient manner.

4.text: SE Question 214: I found Ulysses ________ and never finished the book, waiting instead to read it with someone else so we could penetrate its meaning together.
4.explanation: 'abstruse' and 'recondite' form the correct pair. 'abstruse' means difficult to understand; incomprehensible; 'recondite' means difficult to penetrate; incomprehensible to one of ordinary understanding or knowledge.

4.text: SE Question 215: Some say that Athens was the ________ of democracy, but these people often forget that slaves and women were still not allowed to vote.
4.explanation: 'apotheosis' and 'paragon' form the correct pair. 'apotheosis' means exaltation to divine status; the highest point of development; 'paragon' means an ideal instance; a perfect embodiment of a concept.

4.text: SE Question 216: When listening to a politician speak, it is hard to distinguish the ________ claims from the authentic ones.
4.explanation: 'specious' and 'spurious' form the correct pair. 'specious' means plausible but false; 'spurious' means plausible but false.

4.text: SE Question 217: Captain Ahab was an ________ captain whose reckless and fearless style ultimate leads to his downfall.
4.explanation: 'audacious' and 'intrepid' form the correct pair. 'audacious' means willing to be bold in social situations or to take risks; 'intrepid' means fearless.

4.text: SE Question 218: Many style guides recommend not using idioms in writing because these ________ expressions are uninteresting and show a lack of imagination on the part of the writer.
4.explanation: 'banal' and 'trite' form the correct pair. 'banal' means repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse; 'trite' means repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse.

4.text: SE Question 219: If we lived forever and life was not ________, do you think we would appreciate life less or more?.
4.explanation: 'ephemeral' and 'transitory' form the correct pair. 'ephemeral' means lasting a very short time; 'transitory' means lasting a very short time.

4.text: SE Question 220: He was economical, spending his money ________ and on items considered essential.
4.explanation: 'frugal' and 'thrifty' form the correct pair. 'frugal' means not spending much money (but spending wisely); 'thrifty' means spending money wisely.

4.text: SE Question 221: Two-years in Manhattan had changed Jenna from an ________ girl from the suburbs to a jaded urbanite, unlikely to fall for any ruse, regardless of how elaborate.
4.explanation: 'artless' and 'ingenuous' form the correct pair. 'artless' means without cunning or deceit; 'ingenuous' means to be naÃ ̄ve and innocent.

4.text: SE Question 222: Taking weekly trips to Vegas, Megan was a ________ whose excesses eventually caught up to her.
4.explanation: 'profligate' and 'spendthrift' form the correct pair. 'profligate' means someone who spends money recklessly or wastefully; 'spendthrift' means one who spends money extravagantly.

4.text: SE Question 223: Helen enjoyed blowing soap bubbles, but Jim regarded this as ________, totally unworthy of a woman with a Ph.D.
4.explanation: 'jejune' and 'puerile' form the correct pair. 'jejune' means immature; childish; 'puerile' means of or characteristic of a child; displaying or suggesting a lack of maturity.

4.text: SE Question 224: Unlike the talented artists in his workshop, Paul had no such bent for the visual medium, so when it was time for him to make a stained glass painting, he ended up with a ________ mosaic.
4.explanation: 'humdrum' and 'prosaic' form the correct pair. 'humdrum' means dull and lacking excitement; 'prosaic' means dull and lacking imagination.

4.text: SE Question 225: Standing forlornly by the window, she ________ for her lost love.
4.explanation: 'languish' and 'pine' form the correct pair. 'languish' means become feeble; 'pine' means to yearn for.

4.text: SE Question 226: Peggy's numerous ________ include wearing mismatched shoes, laughing loudly to herself, and.
4.explanation: 'foible' and 'idiosyncrasy' form the correct pair. 'foible' means a behavioral attribute that is distinctive and peculiar to an individual; 'idiosyncrasy' means a behavioral attribute that is distinctive and peculiar to an individual.

4.text: SE Question 227: If Arthur's dog is not fed adequately, he becames highly ________, even growling at his own shadow.
4.explanation: 'choleric' and 'irascible' form the correct pair. 'choleric' means prone to outbursts of temper; easily angered; 'irascible' means quickly aroused to anger.

4.text: SE Question 228: Steve Jobs is surely one of the most ________ CEOs, making Apple the most recognizable and valuable companies in the world.
4.explanation: 'perspicacious' and 'sagacious' form the correct pair. 'perspicacious' means acutely insightful and wise; 'sagacious' means having good judgement and acute insight.

4.text: SE Question 229: Her unbecoming dress was very ________ when it came to her sense of fashion.
4.explanation: 'cogent' and 'telling' form the correct pair. 'cogent' means clear and persuasive; 'telling' means significant and revealing of another factor.

4.text: SE Question 230: Since climate change policy has been mired in congressional fighting, this ________ should help set the goals for president's next term.
4.explanation: 'pinnacle' and 'summit' form the correct pair. 'pinnacle' means the highest point; 'summit' means a meeting of high-level leaders.

4.text: SE Question 231: At first I thought my niece was ________, but I then found myself buying her ice cream every time we passed a shop.
4.explanation: 'artless' and 'guileless' form the correct pair. 'artless' means without cunning or deceit; 'guileless' means free of deceit.

4.text: SE Question 232: The manager spent an hour ________ the employee in the hopes that he would not make these mistakes again.
4.explanation: 'excoriate' and 'objurgate' form the correct pair. 'excoriate' means to criticize very harshly; 'objurgate' means express strong disapproval of.

4.text: SE Question 233: ________ and depressed, Alexei Alexandrovich walked two miles home in the rain after learning that his wife was having an affair.
4.explanation: 'dolorous' and 'lachrymose' form the correct pair. 'dolorous' means showing sorrow; 'lachrymose' means showing sorrow.

4.text: SE Question 234: At first the soccer players bantered back and forth, but as soon as one of the players became ________, calling the other's mother a water buffalo, the ref whipped out a red card.
4.explanation: 'degrade' and 'demean' form the correct pair. 'degrade' means reduce in worth or character, usually verbally; 'demean' means to insult; to cause someone to lose dignity or respect.

4.text: SE Question 235: There is a ________ of jobs hiring today that require menial skills, since most jobs have either been automated or outsourced.
4.explanation: 'dearth' and 'paucity' form the correct pair. 'dearth' means a lack or shortage; 'paucity' means a lack of something.

4.text: SE Question 236: After the relatively small homerun totals in the "dead ball" era, Babe Ruth's homerun totals were truly ________: every year, he set a new all-time record.
4.explanation: 'portentous' and 'prodigious' form the correct pair. 'portentous' means ominously prophetic; 'prodigious' means so great in size or force or extent as to elicit awe.

4.text: SE Question 237: An avid numismatist, Harold ________ amassed a collection of coins from over 100 countries--an endeavor that took over fifteen years, and to five continents.
4.explanation: 'diligent' and 'sedulous' form the correct pair. 'diligent' means characterized by care and perseverance in carrying out tasks; 'sedulous' means done diligently and carefully.

4.text: SE Question 238: In the 1920s, the World Series was rigged--an ________ act which baseball took decades to recover from.
4.explanation: 'base' and 'ignoble' form the correct pair. 'base' means the lowest, class were without any moral principles; 'ignoble' means dishonorable.

4.text: SE Question 239: In an effort to fight ________, the president of the college introduced a new, stricter grading system.
4.explanation: 'apathy' and 'indifference' form the correct pair. 'apathy' means an absence of emotion or enthusiasm; 'indifference' means the trait of seeming not to care.

4.text: SE Question 240: Since old grandpa Harry became very ________ during the summer when only reruns were on T.V., the grandkids learned to hide from him at every opportunity.
4.explanation: 'bellicose' and 'contentious' form the correct pair. 'bellicose' means warlike; inclined to quarrel; 'contentious' means likely to argue.

4.text: SE Question 241: Even a basic understanding of physics can ________ most high schools students.
4.explanation: 'circumvent' and 'elude' form the correct pair. 'circumvent' means cleverly find a way out of one's duties or obligations; 'elude' means escape understanding.

4.text: SE Question 242: Steven was a ________ reader, sometimes finishing two novels in the same day.
4.explanation: 'ravenous' and 'voracious' form the correct pair. 'ravenous' means extremely hungry; devouring or craving food in great quantities; 'voracious' means very hungry; approaching an activity with gusto.

4.text: SE Question 243: When Herb bought football tickets for a game on the day of their wedding anniversary, Jill was ________.
4.explanation: 'exasperate' and 'incense' form the correct pair. 'exasperate' means to irritate intensely; 'incense' means make furious.

4.text: SE Question 244: In her recent book, the author ________ several genres--the detective story, the teen thriller, and the vampire romance--to create a memorable read.
4.explanation: 'coalesce' and 'conflate' form the correct pair. 'coalesce' means fuse or cause to grow together; 'conflate' means mix together different elements or concepts.

4.text: SE Question 245: The CEO refused to ________ on the decision to merge our department with another one, and so I quit.
4.explanation: 'elaborate' and 'expound' form the correct pair. 'elaborate' means explain in more detail; 'expound' means add details or explanation; clarify the meaning; state in depth.

4.text: SE Question 246: Frank came from a ________ enviroment, so he was shocked that his college rooommate sold narcotics.
4.explanation: 'decorous' and 'staid' form the correct pair. 'decorous' means characterized by good taste in manners and conduct; 'staid' means characterized by dignity and propriety.

4.text: SE Question 247: After losing everything in a fire, Tim decided to live in ________ conditions, sleeping on the floor and owning as little furniture as a possible.
4.explanation: 'austere' and 'spartan' form the correct pair. 'austere' means harsh in manner of temperament; 'spartan' means unsparing and uncompromising in discipline or judgment; practicing great self- denial.

4.text: SE Question 248: Youtube is great place to learn just about anything--an expert ________ finer points so that even a complete novice can learn.
4.explanation: 'crystallize' and 'elucidate' form the correct pair. 'crystallize' means cause to take on a definite and clear shape; 'elucidate' means make clearer and easier to understand.

4.text: SE Question 249: Compared to Juliet's passionate concern for human rights, Jake's non-stop concern about football seems somewhat ________.
4.explanation: 'flippant' and 'frivolous' form the correct pair. 'flippant' means showing inappropriate levity; 'frivolous' means not serious in content or attitude or behavior.

4.text: SE Question 250: Mother Anna was always on guard against any ________ from her children and scolded them immediately if any of them talked out of place in public.
4.explanation: 'gaffe' and 'solecism' form the correct pair. 'gaffe' means a socially awkward or tactless act; 'solecism' means a socially awkward or tactless act.

4.text: SE Question 251: The coach suggested improvements Sarah might make on the balance beam, but she remained ________, unwilling to modify any of the habits that made her successful in the past.
4.explanation: 'obdurate' and 'obstinate' form the correct pair. 'obdurate' means stubbornly persistent in changing an opinion or action; 'obstinate' means resistant to guidance or discipline; stubbornly persistent.

4.text: SE Question 252: The colonel was so ________ about enforcing regulations that men fell compelled to polish even the soles of their shoes.
4.explanation: 'meticulous' and 'punctilious' form the correct pair. 'meticulous' means marked by extreme care in treatment of details; 'punctilious' means marked by precise accordance with details.

4.text: SE Question 253: The censor ________ every reference to sex and drugs, converting the rapper's raunchy flow into a series of bleeps.
4.explanation: 'bowdlerize' and 'expurgate' form the correct pair. 'bowdlerize' means edit by omitting or modifying parts considered indelicate; 'expurgate' means to remove objectionable material.

4.text: SE Question 254: I did not expect the insurance agent to give us any straight answers, but I was pleasent surprised by how ________ he was.
4.explanation: 'candid' and 'forthright' form the correct pair. 'candid' means a straightforward and honest look at something; 'forthright' means characterized by directness in manner or speech; without subtlety or evasion.

4.text: SE Question 255: I don't like romanticism for the same reason I don't like melodramatic acting and soap operas--overly ________.
4.explanation: 'mawkish' and 'sentimental' form the correct pair. 'mawkish' means overly sentimental to the point that it is disgusting; 'sentimental' means effusively or insincerely emotional, especially in art, music, and literature.

4.text: SE Question 256: criticized his actions as ________.
4.explanation: 'foolhardy' and 'rash' form the correct pair. 'foolhardy' means marked by defiant disregard for danger or consequences; 'rash' means marked by defiant disregard for danger or consequences; imprudently incurring risk Although Bruce was able to make the delivery in time with a nightime motorcycle ride in the rain, Susan.

4.text: SE Question 257: Dennis arranged an elaborate ________, involving 14 different people lying for him in different situations, so that it could appear that he was meeting Mary completely by chance at the wedding reception.
4.explanation: 'gambit' and 'ploy' form the correct pair. 'gambit' means a manuveur or risk in a game or conversation, designed to secure an advantage; 'ploy' means a clever plan to turn a situation to one's advantage.

4.text: SE Question 258: During the rain delay, many who had come to see the game ________, probably hoping that idle chatter would make the time go by faster.

4.text: SE Question 259: The mothers of the kidnapped victims ________ to the rogue government to release their children, claiming that the detention violated human rights.

4.text: SE Question 260: My sister used to ________ tell me to do the dishes, a chore I would either do perfunctorily or avoid doing altogether.

4.text: SE Question 261: I wanted to spend a week in New York this autumn, but the high costs of travel and lodging ________ my plans.

4.text: SE Question 262: Hoping to sound intelligent, Mary spoke in ________ English that was right out of Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice--needless to say, she didn't have many friends.

4.text: SE Question 263: Jill presented a rather superficial treatment of sales in Asia, but her ________ analysis of sales in Europe inspired a number of insights into how to proceed in that market.
4.explanation: 'efficacious' and 'trenchant' form the correct pair. 'efficacious' means producing the intended result; 'trenchant' means characterized by or full of force and vigor; having keenness and forcefulness and penetration in thought, expression, or intellect.

4.text: SE Question 264: Bob took a risk walking into the "Students Barbershop"--in the end he had to ________ the apparently drunk barber for giving him an uneven bowl cut.
4.explanation: 'reproach' and 'upbraid' form the correct pair. 'reproach' means to express criticism towards; 'upbraid' means to reproach; to scold.

4.text: SE Question 265: Ironically, the leading ________ of Flat-Earth Theory flies all over the world in an effort to win more adherents.
4.explanation: 'advocate' and 'proponent' form the correct pair. 'advocate' means a person who pleads for a cause or propounds an idea; 'proponent' means a person who pleads for a cause or propounds an idea.

4.text: SE Question 266: When Maria reported that she had been visited by Jesus Christ and had proof, a ________ of reporters.

4.text: SE Question 267: In the days leading up to war, a nation typically breaks up into the two opposing camps: doves, who do their best to avoid war, and ________, who are only too eager to wave national flags from their vehicles and vehemently denounce those who do not do th.
4.explanation: 'chauvinist' and 'jingoist' form the correct pair. 'chauvinist' means a person who believes in the superiority of their group; 'jingoist' means a person who thinks that their country should be at war.

4.text: SE Question 268: The man's driver's license was ________ after his tenth car accident, which meant he would never be allowed to legally drive again.
4.explanation: 'countermand' and 'rescind' form the correct pair. 'countermand' means a contrary command cancelling or reversing a previous command; 'rescind' means cancel officially.

4.text: SE Question 269: Count Rumford ________ the new theory of heat, demonstrating that it was wholly inadequate to explain the observations.
4.explanation: 'belittle' and 'denigrate' form the correct pair. 'belittle' means lessen the importance, dignity, or reputation of; 'denigrate' means charge falsely or with malicious intent; attack the good name and reputation of someone.

4.text: SE Question 270: He ________ his subpar performance on the test to a combination of stress and poor sleep.
4.explanation: 'ascribe' and 'impute' form the correct pair. 'ascribe' means attribute or credit to; 'impute' means attribute (responsibility or fault) to something.

4.text: SE Question 271: Each August, when the winds moved in a south easterly direction, the garbage dump would spread ________ vapors through the small town.
4.explanation: 'malodorous' and 'noisome' form the correct pair. 'malodorous' means having an unpleasant smell; 'noisome' means having an extremely bad smell.

4.text: SE Question 272: Some believe people that amassing as much wealth as possible is the meaning to life--yet they often realize that ________ brings anything but happiness.
4.explanation: 'avarice' and 'cupidity' form the correct pair. 'avarice' means greed (one of the seven deadly sins); 'cupidity' means greed for money.

4.text: SE Question 273: To say that Gandhi's actions were ________ is the greatest understatement; he overthrew an empire without violence.
4.explanation: 'commendable' and 'laudable' form the correct pair. 'commendable' means worthy of high praise; 'laudable' means worthy of high praise.

4.text: SE Question 274: Nelly felt the Quiz Bowl director acted ________ towards the underclassmen; really, she fumed, must he act so preternaturally omniscient each time he intones some obscure fact--as though everybody knows that Mt.

4.text: SE Question 275: Despite all the criticism directed at the President during this scandal, Lisa has remained his ________ supporter.
4.explanation: 'robust' and 'stalwart' form the correct pair. 'robust' means sturdy and strong in form, constitution, or construction; 'stalwart' means dependable; inured to fatigue or hardships.

4.text: SE Question 276: Lilian could not help herself from being ________, commenting that the Queen's shoes were showing too much toe.

4.text: SE Question 277: The Ivy League is considered the ________ of the secondary education system.
4.explanation: 'acme' and 'apex' form the correct pair. 'acme' means the highest point of achievement; 'apex' means the highest point.

4.text: SE Question 278: While the literary critic subjected most of the classics to the harshest reviews, he regarded Cervantes as ________, and had nothing but praise for him.

4.text: SE Question 279: The Spanish were forced to ________ much of the territory they had previously conquered.
4.explanation: 'cede' and 'concede' form the correct pair. 'cede' means relinquish possession or control over; 'concede' means give over; surrender or relinquish to the physical control of another.

4.text: SE Question 280: No child has the ________ to go in the rundown house at the end of the street and see if it is haunted.
4.explanation: 'audacity' and 'temerity' form the correct pair. 'audacity' means aggressive boldness in social situations; 'temerity' means fearless daring.

4.text: SE Question 281: The signals were at first ________, but now we detect a clear, consistent pattern of electromagnetic radiation eminating from deep space.
4.explanation: 'intermittent' and 'sporadic' form the correct pair. 'intermittent' means stopping and starting at irregular intervals; 'sporadic' means recurring in scattered and irregular or unpredictable instances.

4.text: SE Question 282: Winston Churchill is famous for many ________, but this might be his most famous: "It has been said that democracy is the worst form of government except all the others that have been tried.".
4.explanation: 'aphorism' and 'apothegm' form the correct pair. 'aphorism' means a short instructive saying about a general truth; 'apothegm' means a short, pithy instructive saying.

4.text: SE Question 283: Schubert was the most ________ composer, producing hundreds of hours of music before he died at the age of 31.
4.explanation: 'fecund' and 'prolific' form the correct pair. 'fecund' means intellectually productive; 'prolific' means intellectually productive.

4.text: SE Question 284: Richard Feynman was renowned for his ________ lectures--the arcana of quantum physics was made lucid as he wrote animatedly on the chalkboard.

4.text: SE Question 285: As soon as he arrived in the city, the ________ young man bought some drugs and headed straight for the seedy parts of town.

4.text: SE Question 286: At one time ________ by math problems, she began avidly "Magoosh-ing", and soon became adept at even combinations and permutations questions.
